clue.text: The weapon of priestly dress in the mass

indicators.note: in tells us the vestment sits inside the crowd word

parts.note: the mass, the common crowd, is the herd
an alb is the white linen vestment a priest wears at Mass

explanation.surface: A question about what weapon lurks among the vestments worn at a church service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mass' tempts towards the church service, chiming with the priest, but here it is the masses, the common crowd; 'in' sets the vestment inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A halberd is a long-shafted axe-and-spike polearm, a weapon carried by medieval foot soldiers.

clue.text: Erred vocally — then got lost?

parts.note: erred is read as said 'er' aloud, a pause in speech, and the proverb says he who pauses in doubt is lost

explanation.walkthrough: 'Erred' is not 'went wrong' but 'said er'; the second half recalls the proverb 'he who hesitates is lost'.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying 'er' is a pause of indecision, and the proverb warns that whoever pauses so is lost.

clue.text: A long time in occupation, like certain Popes

indicators.note: in places the age word inside the job word

parts.note: one's line is one's line of work, a trade
an eon is an immensely long age

explanation.surface: Someone holds a post for ages, as some pontiffs have done.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Occupation' suggests a military takeover; it is LINE of work, holding EON.
explanation.definitionFit: Popes named Leo, thirteen of them, are described by this adjective.

clue.text: Symbolizes Scotsmen when airborne?

definitions.meaning: to represent or convey something
the Flying Scotsman is a famous fast London-to-Edinburgh train, so flying Scotsmen are fast trains

explanation.walkthrough: The Flying Scotsman is the famous London-to-Edinburgh express train, so 'Scotsmen when airborne' are fast trains.
explanation.definitionFit: To symbolize is to convey or represent; and Flying Scotsmen are famous fast trains.

clue.text: Appreciates accommodation

definitions.meaning: slang: to dig something is to like it
British informal word for rented lodgings

explanation.walkthrough: In British use, 'digs' are rented rooms, typically a student's lodgings.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for likes or enjoys, and British informal for lodgings or rented rooms.

clue.text: Left, right — the military dance

definitions.meaning: a marcher's left foot then right foot makes a pair of paces
the Military ... is an old-time ballroom dance

explanation.walkthrough: The drill-sergeant's 'Left, right' is literally a pair of steps; the second reading names the old-time ballroom dance called the Military Two-Step.
explanation.definitionFit: Marching left then right takes a pair of paces, and the military variety is a named old-time ballroom dance.

clue.text: What Thespians need to play Troilus and Cressida

definitions.text: What Thespians need to play Troilus and Cressida

parts.words: What Thespians need to play Troilus and Cressida
parts.note: the play is named after its two lovers, so actors must take those named parts

explanation.walkthrough: Shakespeare's play is named after its two central characters, so the actors playing them take the parts named in its heading.
explanation.definitionFit: Lead parts named in a play's heading, here the two lovers of Shakespeare's drama.

clue.text: Stand and deliver.

parts.note: not a highwayman's demand but standing on a platform to deliver a speech

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is the highwayman's cry, but here an orator stands up and delivers a speech.
explanation.definitionFit: To orate is to give a formal speech, typically standing before an audience.

clue.text: Four in trouble, fiddling

indicators.note: in puts the Roman numeral inside the word for trouble

parts.note: a trial is a trouble or ordeal
IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Four people in a spot of bother over something petty.
explanation.walkthrough: The OCR gave 'hauling'; the smudged page reads 'fiddling', meaning petty. 'In' puts the Roman numeral inside the ordeal word.
explanation.definitionFit: Fiddling in the sense of petty and unimportant: of no consequence.

clue.text: Pride oneself about being in prison

indicators.note: being in tells us the short word goes inside the jail word

parts.note: pen is US slang for a penitentiary, a prison
re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: A prisoner takes pride in themselves while locked up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pen' as prison is a US slang shortening of penitentiary; 'being in' puts the short word for 'about' inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To preen oneself is to congratulate oneself, take smug satisfaction.

clue.text: Plunge quietly, after second attempt to win

indicators.note: after places the soft-music sign behind the other two pieces

parts.note: to woo is to try to win someone's affection
P (piano) is the musical marking for quietly

explanation.surface: A gambler goes all in, quietly, once their second try at winning comes round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Attempt to win' sounds like a bet or a race, but it means courting: WOO. P for quietly comes after S plus WOO.
explanation.definitionFit: To swoop is to plunge suddenly downward, as a hawk dives on its prey.

clue.text: Bowl-navigating New Yorker

definitions.meaning: in the nursery rhyme, three wise men of the English village of Gotham went to sea in a bowl
Gotham is a nickname for New York City, so a resident takes this name

explanation.walkthrough: Gotham is a village in Nottinghamshire whose 'wise men', in the nursery rhyme, went to sea in a bowl; Washington Irving borrowed the name for New York City.
explanation.definitionFit: A resident of the Nottinghamshire village of rhyme, or of the city nicknamed after it, both carry this demonym.

clue.text: Races set back to include woman's start

indicators.note: to include tells us the reversed word wraps around the next piece
set back asks for the little word to be read from right to left

parts.note: taken as written, then turned round
in Genesis, Eve was made from one of Adam's ribs, so a rib was where woman started

explanation.surface: Sporting events are postponed so that a women's start can be added.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Woman's start' looks like a W, but it points to Genesis: Eve began as Adam's RIB. 'Set back' gives TES, and 'to include' puts RIB inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Races in the sense of peoples or ethnic groups are tribes.

clue.text: This glass for a gondolier, no doubt

definitions.meaning: fine glassware from Murano, near Venice, is known by the city's adjective
gondoliers ply the canals of Venice, so one is almost certainly a native

explanation.walkthrough: One reading is the famous Murano glassware; the other is the person who would most likely be poling a gondola.
explanation.definitionFit: Murano glassware takes the city's adjective, and a gondolier is almost certainly a citizen of that lagoon city.

clue.text: Candy canes, tossed about, sway

indicators.note: things tossed about are thrown into disorder, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Christmas sweets thrown around and swaying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sway' looks like a verb of motion, but it is the noun: dominance.
explanation.definitionFit: Sway as a noun is controlling influence, dominance over others.

clue.text: They're more down-to earth than kilts

definitions.text: They're more down-to earth than kilts

parts.words: They're more down-to earth than kilts
parts.note: down-to-earth means literally reaching the ground: Scottish tartan trousers come further down the leg than a kilt does

explanation.walkthrough: 'Down-to-earth' usually means unpretentious; here it is literal, garments that reach nearer the ground than a kilt.
explanation.definitionFit: Trews are close-fitting tartan trousers, a Scottish alternative to the knee-length kilt.

clue.text: Rapidly increases preparations for a winter offensive

definitions.meaning: a problem that grows faster and faster is said to roll up like a ball of snow
packed balls of snow are the ammunition for a winter fight

explanation.walkthrough: The 'winter offensive' sounds like a military campaign, but it is a playground snow fight.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means grows at an accelerating rate; the plural noun is the ammunition stockpiled for a snow fight.

clue.text: Such an agreement needed for a football match

definitions.text: Such an agreement needed for a football match

parts.words: Such an agreement needed for a football match
parts.note: a match needs two sides, as does an accord between two parties

explanation.walkthrough: A football match needs two sides, just like a treaty signed by two parties.
explanation.definitionFit: An adjective for anything involving two sides, as both a two-party treaty and a match between teams do.

clue.text: He takes no active part in 'this, publication

definitions.meaning: an onlooker who watches without joining in
A long-running British weekly magazine

explanation.walkthrough: The Spectator is a long-running British weekly political magazine.
explanation.definitionFit: An onlooker watches without participating; and a British weekly magazine carries this title.

clue.text: Decorate with gold, to stop a row

parts.note: to dam a river is to stop its flow
a row, a noisy quarrel, is a scene

explanation.surface: Gilding something to prevent an argument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' looks like a line, but it rhymes with 'cow': a public quarrel, a SCENE.
explanation.definitionFit: To damascene metal is to inlay it with gold or silver patterns, a craft named after Damascus.

clue.text: Gruesome fly, found in the sea off Napoli

indicators.note: found in means the vehicle is set inside the Italian sea word

parts.note: mare is Italian for sea, and Napoli is Naples
a fly was a light horse-drawn hackney carriage, a cab

explanation.surface: A grisly insect is discovered in the Bay of Naples.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fly' is not an insect but an old one-horse hackney carriage; 'found in' sets it inside the Italian word for sea, Napoli being Naples.
explanation.definitionFit: Macabre means grim and horrifying, dwelling on death.

clue.text: Detached and relaxed

definitions.meaning: a page that has come away from its binding is no longer fixed
slack, not tight or rigid

explanation.definitionFit: Something come away from its fixing is unattached, and a slack, easy posture is free of tension.

clue.text: Unseat the upper class ?

definitions.meaning: to throw someone from their place or overturn them
read as over plus set, the set of people above everyone else

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark asks for a split: OVER plus SET, the class of people above.
explanation.definitionFit: To unseat is to overturn or upset; and the set of people above is the 'over' set.

clue.text: Mounting attack after new deal, leads ace

indicators.note: a fresh deal of the cards shuffles them, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Card-table drama: after the redeal, a player leads an ace and goes on the attack.
explanation.walkthrough: The card-game picture hides the anagram: 'after new deal' rearranges LEADS ACE.
explanation.definitionFit: An escalade is an assault scaling a fortress wall with ladders, an attack made by mounting.

clue.text: Sees a disturbance — tempers apparent

indicators.note: a disturbance throws things out of order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone sees trouble breaking out, and tempers flare in plain view.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tempers' looks like a noun, the angry moods of the surface; it is a verb, moderates. 'Apparent' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To temper something is to moderate or soften it, to relieve its severity.

clue.text: Sloshed on about two pints — rather less, in fact

definitions.text: two pints — rather less, in fact

indicators.note: on means the second piece is put after the first

parts.note: lit is slang for drunk, as is sloshed
re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: Drunk on nearly a quart of beer, though in truth a bit less.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' is a charade indicator here: the 'about' word goes on after the slang for drunk. The definition is fair because a litre is about 1.76 pints.
explanation.definitionFit: The metric unit is about 1.76 imperial pints, a little under a quart.

clue.text: This way is shortened to include the gallows

indicators.note: to include means the abbreviation is opened to take the gallows word

parts.note: the road-type 'this way' names, cut down, is the usual address abbreviation ST
the gallows tree was the old name for the hanging frame

explanation.surface: A road that has been cut short so as to take in a gibbet.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition does double duty with the wordplay: 'this way' abbreviated is ST, which takes in TREE, an old word for the gallows.
explanation.definitionFit: A town road is a thoroughfare, a public way.

clue.text: Criminal set

definitions.meaning: British slang for corrupt or dishonest, as of a crooked policeman
determined, as in being intent on a course

explanation.walkthrough: 'Set' as in 'set on doing it', determined.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for crooked or corrupt, and set in the sense of determined, as in 'intent on'.

clue.text: Means understanding?

definitions.meaning: a person of means has wealth, as in a man of real worth
split as under-standing it gives Latin sub (under) and a stance (a standing)

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark asks for 'understanding' to be split: SUB is Latin 'under', STANCE is a standing.
explanation.definitionFit: A person of means is a person of wealth; and 'under-standing' renders the Latin sub plus a stance.

clue.text: Put back the fifth letter among the others

indicators.note: among places the single letter inside the word for everyone else

parts.note: the rest are all the others
E is the fifth letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: Replacing the fifth letter in its place with the rest of them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The fifth letter' is the fifth of the alphabet, E, placed inside REST.
explanation.definitionFit: To reset a bone or a clock is to put it back into position.

clue.text: View from flats in the Haymarket?

definitions.meaning: a landscape or prospect seen from a viewpoint
flats are painted stage panels, and the Haymarket is a London theatre

explanation.walkthrough: 'Flats' are not apartments but painted canvas panels on stage; the Theatre Royal, Haymarket is a London West End theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: A landscape is a view; and painted stage panels (flats) in a theatre make up the stage set.

clue.text: A heavenly old thing with TV

definitions.text: A heavenly old thing with TV

parts.words: A heavenly old thing with TV
parts.note: heavenly means in the sky: the 1962 communications satellite that first relayed live television across the Atlantic

explanation.walkthrough: 'Heavenly' suggests angels; it means orbiting in the heavens, and 'old' dates it to the early 1960s.
explanation.definitionFit: Telstar was the pioneering 1962 communications satellite that relayed the first live transatlantic television pictures.
